artboards.title: As it stands today — a spreadsheet with a form on top
Proposed — the position, the concentration, and what the price changes cost
Proposed — by supplier, and commission put back in its place
Proposed — nothing bought, nothing to compare with, and a failed read

annotations.text:
THE JOB OF THIS SCREEN

You told me four things in the interview, and everything on the artboard to the right follows from them.

1. YOU ASK IT ALL FOUR QUESTIONS: is a price going up, where is my money going, what did a rise actually cost me, and am I owed commission. Four questions cannot each have a panel -- that is how a screen becomes a dashboard nobody reads. So they are answered in one shape: the STRIP is where the money went, the CHART is who it went to, the RANKING is what the changes cost, and commission is a column on the supplier view where it belongs.

2. THE ORDER IS THE DESIGN. Today the screen ranks on total spend, which only ever answers question two. It now ranks on WHAT THE PRICE CHANGE ADDED TO THIS PERIOD'S BILL, in shillings -- because a percentage cannot be prioritised. Binding wire moved +14.5% and cost you 345,600. Nails moved +4.1% and cost you 113,400. Ranked by percentage you look at the wire; ranked by money you also see that paint at +2.4% cost you 117,300, more than the nails. The money is the answer; the percentage is the evidence for it.

3. EVIDENCE, NOT A VERDICT -- the same stance Sales analytics settled on. No findings queue, no badges, no advice. The one thing it does is DECLARE ITS ORDER in the panel header, so you can argue with it.

4. ONE CHART, AND IT IS CONCENTRATION. Not a spend-per-day chart: purchases are lumpy by nature and thirty bars of a restock pattern is noise wearing a chart's clothes. Concentration is the thing a table genuinely cannot show -- that one man is 36.8% of your buying, and three of them are 76.2% of it. Monochrome on purpose: it is read as length.

Everything is drawn from index.html's own values: the 23-colour palette, the 11/12/13/14/19 ramp, Inter + Archivo Black + IBM Plex Mono, and the .ow-* console components already shipping on Today, Analysis, Debtors, Pricing, Consignment, Creditors and Sales analytics. No new colour, no new weight, no new type size, no fourteenth button family.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT AS IT STANDS >
The eight markers on the artboard.

1. A 240-CHARACTER PARAGRAPH, UNMEASURED, OPEN ON EVERY VISIT. It runs the full 1,110px of the panel. Eight screens already put the long version behind the "i" bubble and keep a one-line sub. This is one of the two left that does not.

2. THE SCREEN'S ONE ACCENT IS SPENT ON A FORM SUBMIT -- and that button is half a lie. Every preset re-renders the moment it is chosen, so "Search" does nothing at all unless you picked Custom. The one real action on the screen, Export CSV, is a ghost button in a corner. This is the identical fault Sales analytics had, and it was fixed there three commits ago.

3. IT IS THE LAST ANALYTICS SCREEN STILL IN THE OLD VOCABULARY. .page-head, .panel, .kpi-grid, .an-subtabs -- 23px 800-weight headings the browser fakes, 12px radii, bordered KPI cards. It sits directly under Sales analytics in the rail and looks like a different application.

4. THE STRIP ANSWERS NOTHING ABOUT PRICE. "Total amt" and "Items bought", and on the supplier tab a third of the top of the screen goes to Expected commission -- which you have just told me is a side note. The screen's actual subject does not appear in its largest type.

5. IT LANDS ORDERED BY TOTAL SPEND. Cement is first because it is the biggest line, which you already knew. Nothing on the screen ranks by movement until you find the right column and click it yourself.

6. THE MOST VALUABLE COLUMN IS THE LAST ONE ON THE RIGHT, AND IT IS A BARE PERCENTAGE. "vs last period" is off the edge of a narrower window, it carries no money, and there is no column anywhere that says what a rise actually cost. +15% on binding wire and +4% on nails: which one do you deal with first? The screen cannot tell you.

7. NINE COLUMNS OF EQUAL WEIGHT. Item name, Variant, Category and Unit are four text columns competing with four money columns, in a fixed-layout table where the item name truncates -- "Iron sheets -- G28, 3m box p..." -- while Variant sits there holding "--".

8. A HORIZONTAL SCROLLBAR, AND NO TOTALS UNTIL YOU HAVE SCROLLED 149 ROWS. The total row is real and it is correct and it is unreachable; the practical way to see what a column adds to is to export it and open a spreadsheet.

AND, ACROSS ALL OF IT: no shape. 33,901,800 spent across 12 suppliers, and nothing anywhere says that one of them is more than a third of it.

THE PROPOSED SCREEN, TOP TO BOTTOM >

THE HEADER. One line of what it is; the paragraph goes behind the "i". The range lives here because it governs every figure below it, and it re-reads on change -- so there is no Search button standing there doing nothing. THE ONE ACCENT IS EXPORT, the only thing on a reading screen there is to do next.

THE STRIP -- four figures, 64px, hairline dividers, no per-tile border. Spent, Purchases, Lines, and then the news: PRICE CHANGES ADDED +1,841,000. It is crimson because a price rise is money leaving, which is the palette's own definition of "genuinely bad", and it is the only crimson on the screen.

Under it, THE BASIS LINE, which is where this screen's honesty already lives and now says all three things out loud: what it is compared with, that seven units cannot be added into one quantity, and that 126 of the 149 lines had no purchase last period so no change is claimed for them.

THE CHART. Sentence first, bar second. "Kato Hardware Supplies is 36.8% of your buying this period." Six steel values from the 23, darkest for the largest, and a three-column legend whose figures line up because they are tabular. Nothing here is a category colour: concentration is length.

THE RANKING, and it declares its order in its own header. Eight columns, the four money ones sized to their content so they can never truncate, the item name told to give way. Colour appears exactly twice: crimson on a rise, verdigris on a fall. "level" and "not bought before" are grey, because a non-answer is not a figure.

TWO THINGS AT THE FOOT THAT THE CURRENT SCREEN GETS WRONG:

The REST IS NAMED. "141 more lines, 1,695,900 spent between them, +175,000 added by their price changes." A truncated list that does not say what it is holding back is a list you cannot trust.

The TOTAL IS AT THE TOP OF THE SCROLL, not 149 rows down -- and three of its six figures are honest dashes. Bags plus kilograms is not a quantity. A price paid does not average across units. A percentage has no total. Money totals, twice, and those are the two that matter.

THE SUPPLIER VIEW, AND WHAT HAPPENED TO COMMISSION >

THE SAME MACHINE. The money columns are identical in kind and position to the item view's, so switching the tab never moves a figure you were reading. Only the identity columns differ.

IT KEEPS THE SPEND ORDER, DELIBERATELY. For a supplier the question is concentration, not movement -- and the chart above has already said who is biggest. This table is that chart with its arithmetic shown, which is why Share is a column here and nowhere else. The header declares the order, as the item view declares its own.

COMMISSION IS A SIDE NOTE NOW, WHICH IS WHAT YOU SAID IT IS. It has lost its tile in the strip and its share of the screen's largest type. What it has NOT lost is a single piece of its honesty:

- A supplier with no rate on file reads "--", never 0. Those are different facts.
- The rate is on the row's meta line, so the projection can be checked rather than taken.
- The total is 1,230,400 with an asterisk, and the asterisk is not decoration. Before this machinery existed the total collapsed the nulls with `Number(x)||0` and printed a figure that counted three rate-less suppliers as earning nothing. The row was honest; the line under it was not.
- The footnote states the uncovered spend as money -- 6,621,800 across 3 suppliers -- and names the fix.

AND THE UNKNOWN SUPPLIER IS A ROW, not a silence. Two purchase invoices with nobody recorded on them, 1,101,800 between them, sitting in the list where they can be seen and fixed.

THE THREE STATES >

A. NOTHING BOUGHT, AND NO STRIP OF ZEROS. Four zeros in 22px mono says the shop is broken. It is not -- so the screen says what it knows instead: 41 purchases worth 28,140,000 in the 30 days before this window, and both reasons a range comes back empty. The second one is the one that actually catches people: goods that arrived without a purchase invoice raised for them do not exist to this screen, and nothing currently says so.

B. NOTHING TO COMPARE IT WITH. This is the state the redesign itself creates, so it is the one it owes you. The screen is now ORDERED on a price change -- and in a shop's first month, or the first time a range is widened past the books, there is no earlier period to change from. It does not print +0. It does not quietly fill the column with dashes and leave the ranking looking deliberate. The tile reads "Not stated" in amber, the header says the order has fallen back to spend, and the panel says why in a sentence. It has NO ACCENT, and that is not an oversight: there is no button that puts a purchase history on a shop that has not bought anything twice yet.

C. THE BOOKS FAILED TO READ. This state does not exist today: when the purchase ledger fails, the screen draws the same empty panel a quiet week draws, and those are not the same news. The app's own law is that a failure must name itself. So it says what failed, at what time, when the last clean read was, and that nothing is being shown from it -- because a figure with no date on it is worse than no figure.

Each of these is a whole screen, so each carries its own single accent. Two of the three have one.

THE PHONE -- a reading fallback, and honest about it >

820px is a switch, not a reflow: 44px navy bar, 26px Archivo page name, 15px row titles, 14-16px padding, cards instead of 38px rows, a white 60px tab bar whose active mark is FILLED rather than merely coloured. No fake status bar and no fake keyboard -- the real ones render on top of this.

WHAT SURVIVES: the 2x2 position in one card with hairline dividers and no per-tile border; the chart's sentence AND its bar, because a single stacked bar is read as length and length still reads at 390 where thirty daily bars would be a smudge; the top three lines by what their price change cost; and the account of what is being held back -- "146 more lines, 14,159,400 spent between them and +313,400 added by their price changes."

WHAT IS DROPPED, DELIBERATELY: the supplier view, the export, the legend, and five of the eight columns. A nine-column table is not read one-handed in a yard, and the screen says so in a line at the bottom rather than pretending it is the whole thing.

THERE IS NO ACCENT ON THIS SCREEN. The accent is the one thing to do next, and on a reading screen with the export dropped there is nothing to do. An oxide button here would have to be pointing at something.
